author: agent:claude-code
message: The lean feature set (todo 01a10ade), built and checked: units, simd and geometry without the `dsp` feature.

check.name: lean build
check.run: cargo test -p autodyne --no-default-features --lib; cargo clippy -p autodyne --no-default-features --lib --tests -- -D warnings; cargo build -p autodyne --no-default-features --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown (CI's no-std job)

title: Lean by default-features = false: one `dsp` feature gates everything beyond units, simd and geometry
body: A new default feature `dsp` declares every module outside units, simd and geometry (and the prelude's DSP re-exports); rustfft, realfft, faer, ndarray, flux and gpu turn it on, so a feature never needs another to make sense. default-features = false is the lean build: units, simd and geometry, no_std. Measured cold wasm32-unknown-unknown release builds: lean 5.1 s (rlib 1.5 MB), no_std with dsp 100 s (14.6 MB; 65 s when measured alone before, this time beside another cargo build). It only adds (rust.features-additive): turning dsp on adds modules and changes nothing in the lean ones. What it changes for users: default-features = false no longer brings the DSP modules; the no_std DSP build is now default-features = false, features = ["dsp"] (woodshed was told the former in its graft answer and needs the feature). Why one feature and not one per area: units, simd and geometry depend on nothing else outside their tests, while the DSP modules use one another throughout (signal under nearly all of them), so per-area features would mostly be the same set with extra cfg; a finer split can come when a user needs one area alone. Integration tests, examples and the dsp bench carry required-features = ["dsp"]; lean CI runs the library's own tests (the doc tests use the DSP modules). Two crate-internal units helpers whose users are all DSP modules (gcd, Lazy) are gated or allowed dead without dsp; the simd tests use a local xorshift instead of osc::Noise, so they run lean too.

title: Declaring the gated modules through a macro broke the crate's exported macros
body: To avoid 29 copies of #[cfg(feature = "dsp")], lib.rs first declared the modules through a macro_rules (`pub mod $m;` per name). The crate's #[macro_export] macros inside those modules then became macro-expanded exports, which can't be named by absolute path (deny-by-default lint macro_expanded_macro_exports_accessed_by_absolute_paths, E in dlpack.rs and dynamic): the dsp build failed. Replaced by one attribute per module. Lesson: never declare modules that hold #[macro_export] macros through a macro; repeat the cfg (or put the gated modules under one parent module if paths may change).
